s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye with optic disc swelling and retinal vascular occlusion
salient_findings: Sudden vision loss in the right eye
Marked swelling of the optic disc
Peripapillary retinal hemorrhages
Occlusion of the superior branch artery
Combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 40s
Presented with blurred vision in the right eye
Undergoing treatment with systemic steroids, durvalumab, and bevacizumab
Initial visual acuity of 20/25 OU
Right eye showed full visual field and relative afferent pupillary defect
Mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination
Normal fundus and visual function in the left eye
MRI showed focal enhancement along enlarged right optic nerve
Lumbar puncture showed no abnormalities
Vitreous biopsy showed hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm
Immunohistochemistry positive for glial fibrillary acid protein and other markers

differentials: Metastatic Disease to the Optic Nerve
per_call: Metastatic Disease to the Optic Nerve

raw.rationale: The presence of a hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm on vitreous biopsy and positive immunohistochemistry for glial fibrillary acid protein and other markers support the diagnosis of a malignant optic glioma.

rejected.label: Central Retinal Artery Occlusion
rejected.why: While the patient did develop occlusion of the central retinal artery, this appears to be a secondary event following the primary pathology of the optic nerve.

rejected.label: Optic Perineuritis
rejected.why: The lack of significant inflammation on imaging and laboratory tests makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Ischemic Optic Neuropathy
rejected.why: The presence of a neoplastic process on biopsy and the pattern of optic nerve involvement are not typical for ischemic optic neuropathy.

rejected.label: Optic Disc Edema
rejected.why: While the patient did have swelling of the optic disc, this is not a diagnosis that explains the full range of findings, including the neoplastic cells on biopsy.
